It leverages sensor data and machine learning to compute P(t), which captures not only whether pressure occurred but also its timing and intensity. This is achieved through a composite of four AI models trained on 90k plays, each contributing to a joint probability distribution. The system assumes discrete player roles and deterministic motion within a bounded temporal window. Dualities emerge between spatial and temporal dimensions—pressure is both a function of immediate physical proximity and cumulative behavioral patterns. Its breakdown regime occurs when data drifts beyond training scope. The identification primitive ensures correct role assignment, forming the basis for all downstream computations. If misidentified, it leads to erroneous state transitions in GSE’s action space.
